seo.og_description: Plan Tetouan: UNESCO white medina, Place Hassan II, kasbah, museums, Martil and a clear north Morocco itinerary.

hero_subtitle: Andalusian white medina under the Rif — crafts, museums and the Mediterranean a short ride away.

info.entry_val: Authentic, walkable, less crowded than Fez

overview.title: A white city that still works as a city
overview.p1: Tetouan sits where the Rif meets the Mediterranean plain, a short hop from Tangier and a natural stop on the way to Chefchaouen. Its UNESCO medina is whitewashed and dense, with a strong Andalusian memory: Spanish street names, workshops that still produce leather and textiles, and a pace slower than Fez or Marrakech.
overview.p2: You come for the medina lanes, Place Hassan II, the kasbah views, two solid museums, and the option of Martil beach when you want salt air. It rewards travellers who like walking cities more than checklist monuments.
overview.p3: Base yourself near the medina or in the Spanish-built extension if you want easier taxis. One full day covers the core; two days let you add Martil and a slower craft trail.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Medina first, museums and kasbah second, sea or mountain third.

day1.title: Medina & Place Hassan II
day1.morning: Enter the medina from Place Hassan II. Walk the main souk axes without rushing — leather, textiles, and food lanes. Climb toward the kasbah for the first elevated view.
day1.afternoon: Archaeological Museum if open, then a slow loop back through quieter residential lanes. Tea on or near the square.
day1.evening: Dinner in the medina or the Spanish quarter. Early night if you plan Martil tomorrow.

day2.title: Museums, palace façades & craft
day2.morning: Modern Art Museum and any temporary shows. Walk the royal palace exterior and the cleaner avenues of the new town.
day2.afternoon: Artisan quarter and workshops — ask before photographing. Mellah lanes if you want a quieter historic pocket.
day2.evening: Sunset viewpoint above the medina if the light is clear. Simple grill dinner.

day3.title: Martil or Rif day
day3.morning: Taxi or local bus to Martil for beach time and seafood. Or start toward Chefchaouen if you are continuing south into the Rif.
day3.afternoon: Swim, walk the corniche, or return to Tetouan for last shopping and a museum you missed.
day3.evening: Pack and connect to Tangier, Chefchaouen, or the coast.

detailed_itinerary.title: Hour-by-hour ideas
detailed_itinerary.subtitle: Flexible blocks you can swap around opening times.
detailed_itinerary.day1_m: Morning — Place Hassan II & medina edge
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start on Place Hassan II while the light is soft, then enter the white medina lanes for crafts and everyday life.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Climb toward the kasbah walls for views over the roofs, then return through quieter residential streets.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Dine near the square or in the ville nouvelle — Tetouan evenings are calmer than Tangier.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Visit the Archaeological Museum for Roman and local finds, then walk toward the Royal Palace facade (exterior only).
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: See the Modern Art Museum, then explore the Mellah quieter fabric before the heat peaks.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: A calm dinner in the centre; keep the night early if you leave for Martil tomorrow.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Artisan quarter or free time
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Return to a favourite medina corner or the artisan lanes without a fixed checklist.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Taxi to Martil for Mediterranean air, a walk on the sand and simple seafood.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: A final stroll on Place Hassan II before continuing toward Tangier, Chefchaouen or the coast.

1.title: Walk the medina with a reset point
1.desc: Use Place Hassan II as your compass. When lanes confuse you, return to the square instead of accepting the first shortcut offer.

2.title: Combine city and sea
2.desc: Martil is close enough for an afternoon. Do the medina and museums first so the beach feels like a reward, not a substitute.

3.title: Spanish still helps
3.desc: Tetouan’s history means Spanish is widely understood alongside Arabic and French — useful in shops and taxis.

transport.title: Getting around without wasting time
transport.desc: The medina and Place Hassan II are walkable. Use petits taxis for Martil or the kasbah heights. Agree the price before you start or insist on the meter.

bargain.title: Shopping and expectations
bargain.desc: Souks are calmer than Fez. Polite bargaining is normal for crafts. Museum tickets and official sites have fixed prices.

water.title: Heat, water and timing
water.desc: Summer afternoons are hot in the lanes. Do the medina and kasbah in the morning, carry water, and keep Martil or museums for later.

q1.question: How many days in Tetouan?
q1.answer: Two days cover medina, museums and kasbah. Add a third for Martil or as a buffer before Chefchaouen.

q2.question: Is Tetouan worth visiting?
q2.answer: Yes if you want a northern medina without Fez intensity — strong craft culture, clear square, and easy links to Tangier and the Rif.

q3.question: Medina or new town stay?
q3.answer: Medina for atmosphere; new town for taxis, AT arrivals and simpler logistics.

q4.question: Safe for solo travellers?
q4.answer: Generally yes in daytime medina and main avenues. Standard city caution at night; use taxis after dark if unsure.

q5.question: Best time to visit?
q5.answer: April–June and September–November for mild weather. Summer is hot inland but fine for Martil beach.
